list: The official 55 trophies, as listed before release (2026-11-18)
note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as published. Every guide below is written in our own words from the official description alone, because the game had not released when this guide was written. Anything beyond the description is marked as inferred, and no mission name, place or step is stated as fact unless the official description itself names it.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the reward for earning the other 54 trophies, and it unlocks automatically the moment the last one pops. Treat it as a checklist rather than a goal of its own: work through this guide's roadmap in order and the platinum takes care of itself. Confirmed by the official description; the order of the roadmap is our own suggestion, built from the descriptions.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play through the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end and this trophy pops. It is unmissable story progress: there is no way to finish the opening without it. The mission name comes from the official description itself. Inferred: as the first mission, it is likely also your introduction to the game's fishing, so take a moment to learn the controls here.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1 and this unlocks when the chapter closes. It is unmissable as long as you keep playing the story; nothing optional is needed. Inferred from the description: chapter trophies in this series have always popped at the chapter's final cutscene, so keep playing until the chapter title card changes.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 in full and this pops at its end. Like the other chapter trophies it is unmissable story progress, earned by playing the main missions in order. Inferred: the chapter's name hints at the story's turn toward the drug trade, so expect the missions here to introduce the money side of the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 and this unlocks as the chapter wraps up. It is unmissable: just keep following the story missions. Inferred from the description and the chapter's name: this is the point where the game fully opens up Vice City itself, so it is a good moment to start the side activities this guide lists under later stages.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4 and this pops at the chapter's end. Unmissable story progress, like the other chapter trophies. Inferred: with four chapters named in the list, Chapter 4 is likely the last full chapter before the finale, so expect the story to narrow toward the final mission from here.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the game's final mission and this gold trophy pops. It is unmissable for anyone who completes the story. Inferred from the description: the name suggests the finale is a choice about when to walk away, so if the game offers a final decision, save before it — the choice itself is not confirmed anywhere yet, and this guide will say so plainly once it is.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run and this pops at its end. It is a named mission trophy, so it unlocks by playing the story in order; if you somehow pass the mission without it, replay it from the mission menu. Inferred: the name suggests an early, low-stakes job — likely a good first mission to learn the game's driving and on-foot controls.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist and this unlocks when it ends. Named-mission trophies come from story progress, so just play the mission when it appears. Inferred from the name: expect a planned robbery against a cartel target, so bring your best weapons and a fast getaway vehicle — the details are not confirmed, and the guide says so rather than inventing them.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play to earn this. It pops on mission completion, so it is unmissable story progress. Inferred from the name alone: the title hints the mission involves family or a younger character — treat that as a guess from the title, not a fact, until the game is out and the guide can be checked.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners and this pops at the end of it. Like every named-mission trophy, it is earned by playing the story in order. Inferred: the stylised title suggests a mission tied to a music act or a headline event in Vice City — a guess from the name only, not a confirmed detail.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown and this unlocks. VCIA is the game's airport, so the mission is tied to that location by its own name — that much is confirmed by the description. Inferred: expect a vehicle or aircraft theft at the airport; the exact target and steps are not confirmed, so this guide does not invent them.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory and this pops when it ends. It is unmissable story progress. Inferred from the name: an operation with a military-sounding title suggests a bigger, set-piece mission — possibly the one tied to the 'unscheduled departure' trophy elsewhere in this list — but the link between the two is a guess, not a confirmed fact.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the game's in-game completion checklist and this gold trophy pops. The checklist itself is not published in the official description, so this guide cannot list its exact items yet — that is stated here rather than guessed. Inferred from the series' history: it usually covers story missions, stranger strands, collectibles and activities, so the other trophies in this guide are a good map of what counts; check the in-game stats page as you play.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts in total — jumps, near-misses, drifts and the like, as the game counts them. The count is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so it builds naturally while you drive around Leonida; do not grind it early. Inferred: stunts in this series usually register on big air, long drifts and close calls, so a fast car and open roads are the practical route, but the exact moves the game counts are not confirmed yet.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of side activity once — PSN tracks 9 activity types. You only need to sample each one, not finish it, so this is quick once you know where the activities are. Inferred: the 9 types are likely the activities named elsewhere in this list (races, fishing, arcade, shooting range, drone races, bowling, meditation, hunting and one more), but the official description does not name them, so treat that list as a working guess.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — the count comes from PSN's own tracking. This is the hardest skill trophy in the list, so leave it for the cleanup stage when you have the best weapons and plenty of practice. Inferred: ranges in this series reward steady aim and headshots over speed, and each challenge likely has its own weapon, so work through them weapon by weapon rather than in one sitting.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — the location count comes from PSN's tracking. Each location needs just one win, so you can tick them off as you find them across the map. Inferred: drone races reward learning each course's line more than raw speed, so replay a course a couple of times before moving on; the locations themselves are not published yet.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different courses, not the same one 20 times. Any race type counts toward the total as long as the course is new to your wins list. Inferred: mix street, off-road and water races if the game offers them, and use the fastest vehicle class for each course; the race list itself is not published, so this guide does not name courses it cannot confirm.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named character in the description, so look for his challenge wherever fishing challenges are offered — likely at a pier or on a boat. Inferred: fishing challenges usually come down to landing the bigger catch or more fish in the time limit, so upgrade your rod and tackle first; whether the challenge repeats if you lose is not confirmed, so try to win it on the first attempt.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish any one arcade game, start to end. One completion is all it takes, so pick the shortest cabinet you find. Inferred: arcade machines are likely found in bars, arcades and similar interiors around Vice City; the specific games are not published, so this guide does not name one it cannot confirm.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand through to his final mission. Character strands unlock as the story progresses, so keep taking Andy's jobs when they appear on the map. Inferred: the name suggests Andy is working through some kind of recovery, so his strand is likely a series of small, personal jobs rather than big heists — a reading of the title only.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's mission strand up to his final mission. Take his jobs as they appear and the trophy pops when the strand ends. Inferred from the title: boats and water are involved, so expect at least one job on the water — a guess from the name, not a confirmed step.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand through to his last mission. Keep accepting Billy's jobs when they show up. Inferred: the title points to a solo rider, so his strand likely centres on bikes — a guess from the name alone, and this guide does not dress it up as fact.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. Strangers appear as markers on the map as you explore, so this is a long, wandering trophy — start it early and take every stranger job you pass. Inferred: there are likely more than 8 strands in the game, so you can pick the easiest eight; the strands themselves are not published, so no names are listed here.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's mission strand through to his final mission. Take Randy's jobs as they appear on the map. Inferred from the title: supply and demand points to moving goods, so his strand likely involves deliveries or deals — a reading of the name only, not a confirmed detail.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand through to his last mission. Accept his jobs whenever they appear. Inferred: the title hints at spinning — wheels, records or a spin of some kind — so his strand may involve driving or music, but that is a guess from the name and this guide does not present it as fact.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida — the count comes from PSN's tracking. Spots are scattered around the map, so this pairs well with the exploration trophy: meditate at each spot as you pass it. Inferred: meditation spots in this series are usually quiet, scenic places, so look for viewpoints, beaches and parks; the exact spots are not published yet.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. MISSABLE — the animal is unique, so there may be only one of it: do not shoot it before Bret's hunt is set up, and save before you take the shot. Inferred: unique-animal hunts in this series usually mean tracking one specific animal to a marked area, so follow Bret's instructions and use a scoped weapon for a clean kill; the animal's species and location are not published.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full sets of collectible cards. Cards are hidden around the world, so this is a slow hunt — pick up every card you pass from the start rather than leaving them all for the end. Inferred: cards are likely grouped into themed sets, and you need every card in a set for it to count, so a map of card locations (not yet published) will be the practical tool once players find them.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It feature at 100 different locations across Leonida. The count is cumulative and locations only count once each, so spread it out as you explore rather than repeating one spot. Inferred: WAiNK It is likely a phone or social feature tied to places — the exact action is not confirmed — so try it at every landmark you pass and watch the counter in the stats page.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges in total. Challenges are the game's small optional goals, and the count builds across every type, so this comes naturally if you sample everything. Inferred: the in-game challenges menu will show what is available and your progress, so check it early and steer toward the quick ones; the full challenge list is not published.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose it completely. MISSABLE in practice — the setup is specific, so plan it: earn the wanted level together, then break line of sight and hide until it clears. Inferred: a quiet stretch of countryside or the water is the easiest place to vanish; do it as a deliberate attempt, not by accident, and keep your partner close the whole time.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without ever losing your wanted level — the level must stay active through all three robberies. MISSABLE per attempt: if the wanted level drops between shops, the chain breaks and you start over. Inferred: pick three shops close together on a quiet street, rob fast, and drive straight to the next one without stopping to fight the police.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. A vehicle counts when you first get in or drive it, so variety is everything — try every car, bike, boat and aircraft you see. Inferred: the counter is cumulative across the whole game, so it builds on its own if you never stick to one car; car meets, docks and airfields are the fastest way to find new types.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. MISSABLE per attempt — one use, five takedowns, so set it up: find a spot with at least five enemies grouped together before you trigger it. Inferred: Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion aiming mode, so a busy shootout with cover nearby is the practical setup; a weaker weapon may not finish five in time, so bring something with punch.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave VCIA — the airport — in an unscheduled way, meaning not through a normal flight. MISSABLE per attempt: the description implies a specific escape, so go to the airport, get a vehicle or aircraft moving, and leave by a route the game does not schedule. Inferred: stealing a plane and taking off, or driving out through a restricted gate, are the likely readings — the exact trigger is not confirmed, so try the boldest exit first.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke about Rhinos — the military tank of this series — and the trophy is tied to them. Inferred: you likely need to steal, drive or survive in a Rhino tank, most plausibly at a high wanted level when the army rolls in. The exact trigger is not published, so this guide does not invent one: get a wanted level high enough for tanks to appear, then deal with the Rhino however you can.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected at any point. MISSABLE per attempt — one sighting ends the run, so plan it: go at a quiet hour, move slowly, and avoid cameras and guards. Inferred: stealth gear and a silent approach matter more than speed here, and if you are spotted, leave and try again rather than fighting through it.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault needs a successful robbery and a clean getaway, so the count is cumulative — one vault at a time is fine. Inferred: bank vaults are likely the biggest robberies in the game, so plan each one like a heist — a fast car parked outside, a route out of the area — and do not attempt two in one wanted level unless you are confident.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape afterwards. Armored trucks drive set routes around the map, so watch for one, stop it, take the cash and get away. Inferred: blocking the road ahead of the truck is the classic move the name nods to, and the getaway matters as much as the robbery — have an escape route before you start.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — the area count comes from PSN's tracking. You need to set foot in every named area on the map, so this is a completionist's road trip. Inferred: the in-game map will show which areas you have visited, so check it after the story and mop up the corners you never passed through; boats and aircraft help with the islands and the far south.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — the gang count comes from PSN's tracking. Each gang's operation is a separate target, so you need nine robberies in total, one per gang. Inferred: illegal operations are likely marked on the map once discovered, so explore gang territory and take each operation as you find it; the gangs themselves are not named in the official description.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail somewhere with a view on Ocean Beach. The description names the place — Ocean Beach — so head to a bar or spot overlooking it and order a drink. Inferred: this is a quiet, scenic moment rather than a challenge, so take it slow and enjoy the view; the exact bar is not published, so any beachfront spot that serves drinks is the sensible first try.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom, in a vehicle, in classic style — the series' famous showroom smash. MISSABLE per attempt: the description implies driving a car straight through the showroom glass, so line up a fast car, aim at the window and go. Inferred: a showroom with a big glass front is the target, and the smash is the whole point — do not stop inside to browse, just drive out through the glass.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley, and follow through on your throw. MISSABLE per attempt — the follow-through is the specific action, so complete the bowling motion properly rather than rushing the throw. Inferred: this is a nod to the series' classic bowling, so a full game at that alley is the safe route; the alley's location is not published yet.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The official description is deliberately vague — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — and the trophy is hidden on PlayStation, so this guide cannot give a verified method yet. Inferred from the wording alone: it likely involves the game's partnership system reaching a wide audience, perhaps a social-media or fame milestone. That is a guess, and this guide marks it as one rather than inventing steps.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a count up to 500, so this is a long, cumulative tally of decisions across the game. It builds as you play: dialogue choices, mission decisions and the like all likely count. Inferred: there is no shortcut to 500 choices, so do not grind it; just play the whole game, take every decision point you find, and let the counter climb.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed on the second try — 'second time's the charm'. MISSABLE in the sense that you need a failed first attempt followed by a success, so it only pops when you fail something and then pass it. Inferred: the natural way is to fail any retryable activity once and then complete it; do not force it early, just keep it in mind the next time you fail a challenge and go straight back in.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: The official description is a reaction — 'what the hell just happened?' — and the trophy is hidden, so no verified method exists yet. Inferred: the name points to something strange or unexplained in the world, likely a random event or a secret encounter. Explore odd corners of the map and take every strange prompt seriously; this guide will name the trigger once players confirm it.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a melee drive-by. MISSABLE per attempt: you need the right speed, the right angle and a target close to the road, so set it up on a busy street. Inferred: a slow drive past a pedestrian with a melee swing is the practical method; do not try it at high speed or you will miss, and expect a wanted level afterwards.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, and your contacts clean them for a cut, so the total builds across the whole game. Inferred: keep laundering every batch of marked bills as soon as you can rather than hoarding them, and the $250,000 total will arrive on its own by the late game.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops. Every purchase counts — clothes, weapons, food, vehicles — so this builds naturally as you play. Inferred: if you reach the late game short of the total, the fastest top-up is expensive weapons or a high-end vehicle; there is no need to grind it early when ordinary shopping does the job.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties — the count comes from PSN's tracking. Garages are bought through the in-game property market, so save up and purchase each one as it appears. Inferred: garages are scattered across Leonida, so check the property listings in each area you visit; the total cost is not published, so keep a healthy bank balance in the late game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is named in the description, so open it on your phone in-game and register vehicles you own or find. Inferred: registration likely means adding a vehicle to the app's list, so drive a variety of vehicles and register each new one as you go; ten is a small total, so this is a quick cleanup trophy.
